To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrostatic sag of a wire can be computed using the Finite Difference Method and that the gravitational sag can be obtained by solving the second-order differential equation.

1) the wire sag can be calculated with high accuracy using the three point Finite Difference method (FDM) and the electrostatic force obtained from the nearly exact Boundary Element method (neBEM), 2) a wire sag of 2.5 mm is expected for a typical RICH chamber, and 3) the gravitational sag is negligible for the RICH chamber.

the wire sag is a complex phenomenon that depends on many parameters, including: (i) the wire length, (ii) the number of wires and the distance between the wires, (iii) the wire tension and (iv) the electric field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for solving the wire deflection in multiwire chambers.
the numerical computation of the wire sag in multiwire chambers.
the numerical computation of electrostatic force on the wire and its application to determine the sag of a wire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the method presented in this thesis is capable of computing the sag of a wire of arbitrary shape in any multiwire chamber.
the sag of wires is a function of the electrostatic force, the gravitational force, and the wire tension.
the wire sag is a function of the electrostatic and gravitational forces and the sag increases with the increase in the wire radius and the decrease in the distance between the wire and the anode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sag in wires of the multiwire chamber is a function of the wire material, its radius, the wire tension, the applied voltage and the chamber geometry.
the electrostatic force is the most important contributor to the sag.
the wire sag is not a significant factor for the ALICE RICH multiwire proportional chambers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gravitational force is negligible compared to electrostatic force.
the electrostatic forces are dominant over the gravitational ones.
the electrostatic sag in a MWPC can be computed accurately by using the neBEM and FDM.
